selection: All four application modules from the frozen prior expansion review; no substitution. Purposeful Python-only feasibility cohort, not representative yield.
protocol: At most five path commits and 20 origin requests per repository, complete Git tree required, 8MiB API/256KiB source caps. Then seven bounded context reads at matched revisions. Rehash every response; compare source SHA256, plain SHA1 and Git blob SHA1; bind notices/context to tree blobs. Read only; no installation or corpus execution.

results.test_linkage: No test-named paths in complete tree. Inspected evaluate_recommender.py scores a different module; it does not check the summarizer.
results.quality_boundary: Unpinned requirements include sklearn; summarizer uses get_feature_names and local JSON. Static reading suggests a top-two ranking defect: a new maximum does not demote the old maximum. No executable correctness claim.

decision: Origin recovery succeeded; none is independently verified or admitted. Do not use test filenames or README coverage as checked-code gates. Close this feasibility packet; next freeze a stratified language/role yield audit with explicit exclusions, dependency/test discovery and independent oracle gates before bulk expansion. Keep natural-code eligibility separate from verified-exercise eligibility.
limitations: Matching revision is not proof of original crawl revision.
MIT notice recovery does not establish complete source-use acceptance.
GitHub fork metadata is not a complete source-family/near-duplicate graph.
Source implementations retain only the prior bounded content screen; newly recovered context is provenance evidence, not screened training payload.
No dependency installation, sandbox execution, derived task generation, full security review, or corpus-scale eligible token estimate.
